posts.text:
Brace yourselves. Over the next few weeks you are going to see a wave of hatred against Elon Musk unlike anything before.

A four-hour hit-piece documentary rolling out nationwide. Midterms three weeks away. Every outlet, every NGO, every “expert” panel suddenly singing from the same sheet, on the same day, with the same words.

None of it is spontaneous.

What you are watching is an organism. Call it international socialism, call it the managerial left, the name doesn’t matter. It is a network that spent decades quietly capturing the universities, the newsrooms, the foundations, the administrative state, every institution that was supposed to referee the game instead of playing it.

For years it worked because no one with real power ever looked under the hood.

Then a man who lands rockets, owns the public square and needs nobody’s permission started looking. And started showing everyone else what he found.

So the organism does what every organism does when it senses a threat to its survival. It screams.

Don’t mistake the noise for strength. What you are about to hear is not the roar of a system in control. It is a death cry.

The louder it gets, the closer he is to the nerve.

I wrote about why this happens, and why “Nazi” is always the weapon of choice 👇

Nearly half a million Indian schools still have no internet. This is exactly the kind of problem Starlink was built to solve

According to India's Education Ministry’s UDISE+ 2025–26 data:

• 1,466,682 schools nationwide
• 989,191 have internet access
• 477,491 still don't have internet
• Only 67.4% of schools are connected

That means nearly one in three schools across India still lacks internet access

This is where Starlink makes a real difference

For schools in remote villages and regions where laying fiber is difficult or expensive, and so they essentially end up with no internet at all, satellite internet brings teachers and students online without waiting for broadband cables to reach every classroom

And Starlink has already demonstrated what this can achieve

In 2025 alone, Starlink connected more than 6 million students worldwide through education initiatives

India has millions of students living far beyond major cities, and connecting underserved schools would open up access to online learning, educational resources, and opportunities that were previously out of reach

A child's access to knowledge should not depend on whether a broadband cable reaches their classroom

This is another powerful reason to bring Starlink connectivity to more schools across India

You just sign into Grok once, and your Bots will be available on all future rides, and automatically logged out when you exit the vehicle to maintain privacy.

I tried it tonight by adding laundry detergent to my Amazon cart. It can also send emails, place your coffee order, manage your calendar, finances, or other tasks using just your voice in the robotaxi.

On your next ride, you’ll automatically be signed in to all the apps you previously logged into as soon as you enter the vehicle.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Starlink is a life-saving technology.

A huge tree crushed a family’s car in the French Alps. A passerby says there was no mobile signal, so he used his @Starlink Mini, mounted on his car, to call emergency services and share GPS coordinates.

Rescuers arrived about 20 minutes later. Firefighters freed the trapped occupants, and all five survived.

A working connection can mean the difference between life and death. Starlink can provide that lifeline when people need it most.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Starlink has an Indian license, 20 ground stations on Indian soil, and a promise to keep Indian user data in India. What it doesn't have is permission to switch on.

Thousands of Indian villages still have no 4G. In the Northeast alone, more than 1,800 had no mobile signal of any kind as of February, most of them in Arunachal Pradesh. These are the places satellite internet is built for: mountain villages, islands, flood zones, anywhere a tower or a fiber line takes years and a lot of money to arrive.

Starlink has done what India asked. It got its telecom license in June 2025 and space regulator approval a month later. It built India-specific security controls, agreed to keep data local, and has been reporting the names, addresses and coordinates of its test terminals to the government every two weeks. It operates in more than 150 countries. In India it still can't sell a single subscription, and the company is now talking about early 2027.

New Delhi says nobody is being singled out, since Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio's satellite venture are stuck at the same stage. I believe that, and I don't think it helps. When three licensed operators, two of them backed by India's biggest telecom groups, can't clear security review after more than a year of trials, that tells you the process has no deadline. It doesn't tell you it's thorough.

The security concerns are real. Indian agencies have been rattled by smuggled terminals turning up in border areas, and India is entitled to lawful interception, local data storage and an emergency shutoff. Starlink has already signed up for all of it. The answer to a misused terminal is enforcement, not keeping the service dark for everyone who would use it legally.

Elon Musk has been blunt, calling the delay "a crime against the people of India" and asking, "Is Ambani the real boss of India?" You don't need to buy the whole oligarch theory to see his point. Reliance spent months lobbying for spectrum auctions that would have favored deep-pocketed incumbents. The government sided with Starlink on that one, which is to its credit. Now it needs to finish the job.

India can keep every security power it wants and still let a kid in Arunachal get online. Right now it's choosing not to.

🚨Conversion Practices Bill: Scrutiny Starts Tomorrow🚨

This Bill is an utter nightmare. It criminalises talking. It will rob children of the opportunity to become comfortable in their own bodies. 

It includes no exemption for parents. Parents who try to dissuade their children from ‘transitioning’ could be criminalised and put in prison for 5 years. 

It enshrines the notion of ‘transgender identity’ in the law and makes the offence ridiculously broad: “conduct causing someone to believe that they have or do not have a transgender identity”.

It further enshrines the notion of being ‘non-binary’ in the law.

The protection for therapists and other medical professionals is severely lacking, with a test of ‘reasonableness’ created. There is also a low threshold for what constitutes ‘abuse’.

Make no mistake about it, this Bill poses a significant threat to freedom of speech, religious freedoms and to the safeguarding of vulnerable children.

It must not be allowed to become law. Please petition your MP.
